I was enjoying it, until the AI art slop-fest started. I was tolerant of it at first, but less so as the art has started to look not so good. The thing is, as consumers, we really have no way of knowing how much AI is being used or how it impacted the employees at a company. We only have your word for staffing levels, and corporations lie all the time, more so when it makes them money. Disclosing it isn't going to win you an award; that's literally required to be on Steam at all. So stating you're being transparent about it in your FAQ doesn't make you a great company. It just means you follow the rules.

The problem with AI art is even when you pay for it, the engines are built of art scraped from the web. Art that does not belong to the AI art generating license people. They are thieves, and even if you pay them for a license, you are still generating art using someone else's hard work and not paying them for it. In any other industry this would be called stealing. Because the laws haven't caught up with AI art yet, you can get away with it, but that doesn't make it right guys. You are profiting off of someone else's hard work and not paying them for it.

Back to Pinball FX for me. While Zen is also greedy, at least they haven't hopped on the AI bandwagon yet.

FWIW, I only made this review because you locked the post talking about AI art in the forums. If it bothers you that people are talking about what you're doing, then you probably did something wrong.

As a pinball simulator, Magic Pixel delivered a great experience. The physics feel good, and the light effects are realistic. The replicated Zaccaria tables from the 70s and 80s are excellent. The retro tables are infuriatingly challenging but in the way you come back for more (I wish/hope Magic Pixel uses this system to recreate some real WWII era tables). The "remake" and "deluxe" tables feel like an attempt to copy Pinball FX's remakes of 90s tables; these are more miss than hit as satisfying tables. The Primal Carnage tables are generally fun, and the zombie addon was more fun than I expected. The menus are not controller friendly, and I have to use a mouse if I want to read table rules while using a game pad. The tournament system has me logging in every day to try and set a top score. Grab this game for accurate and exciting retro pinball--especially tables that are difficult to find in arcades today.

First off, I do want to say I understand people's feelings on the A.I. art on what is now a majority of the tables. Even as I don't hate A.I. but also think it's being used in pretty awful and lazy ways, I'm not going to contend with the many valid views and arguments there are against it, or the ones that are just blind flailing, for separate reasons. But, like it or not, it it does represent a majority of what you will be looking at if you get the sum total of tables the game has, which are all pretty fantastic to play.

I've been looking at real and digital pinball playfields for about 35 years now, and the A.I. art here achieves it's own sort of uncanny valley. Most of the tables are fine, art wise, some of them are weird, especially those where there are floor targets that are supposed to match up with some art asset and are clearly off-set from what we actually get.

HOWEVER. The developers have provided in-game tools to replace the art as you see fit, and while I haven't gone out of my way to do so yet myself, I'm sure someone has been creatively angry enough to come up with their own art for the tables out there, or even restore the art that had been on a lot of the tables once upon a time.

ALSO. All of the real tables that the O.G. Zaccaria pinball company actually made have all of their original, 100% human drawn art and all the jank that went with the tables' respective era. It was always jank, we just have a new kind now.

As for the tables themselves? There isn't a better suite out there. Forget ZEN. Arcade trash. Which is sad because they are the license holders of some of the best tables in history.

I digress.

You have every possible era of pinball represented here: OG Boardwalk impossible tables, the slightly moderen EM tables, The subtle flavors of Solid State progression, The modern digital era, the retro EM, the 'grandma got this at Walmart because she remembered you liked the vidya' era. I don't know what other flavor of pinball they could add except pachinko, plinko, those things you used to get in Cracker Jack when it didn't suck, and Wonderful Waterfuls (for anyone that needed an age verification).

And they all play beautifully, reactively, and you don't need $4k in computer hardware to make it look good or run smooth. I've played this on an eight year old Acer Nitro 5, a 2060ti, and higher grade hardware. You may not get full ray tracing on old hardware, but it will still be a fantastic play. It sort of feels like the natural torch receiver from the old Pinball Arcade from Farsight. The room got shinier, the tables all changed, but the same level of love for real tables is in there.

I know the developer's explanation, but it's a fact that they're constantly advertising the Achievement Table Pack, while at the same time, for months, they've been removing hundreds of achievements because of the 5,000 achievement limit.

I'm a pinhead that paid 40 USD to support this developer when this package looked like it might eventually turn into something worth owning. 

Good grief did I ever make a mistake. This has become complete trash, free to play, AI generated slop with a comical amount of redundant, valueless DLC. The tables I originally purchased in the Gold pack were (apparently) not affected but it's hard to be happy about that considering the way development of the game has regressed.

I looked at about two dozen of the recently released tables and they all look like copypasta garbage with piss poor AI generated art. Pinball isn't about different table art with the same basic underlying table every time (unless you're exclusively a fan of pre-1970s pinball and even then those older tables at least occasionally had some innovative ideas). Most of the new Zaccaria tables could have been designed by a random number generator: 3 pop bumpers this time instead of 4, 4 rollover lanes this time instead of 3, move a few elements around so they aren't in exactly the same place as last time, change the letters on the spot targets, blah blah blah. And so many of these tables are obviously just reskins without even the aforementioned limited work put in to make them APPEAR different! You can go online and download fan created tables in VPX/FP/etc that have far more originality, effort, and playability in them and they're FREE.

And the AI generated art is a terrible design choice for a team dedicated to pushing out as many bland and soulless pinball tables as possible. It's incredibly cynical and genuinely makes me sad. All of it does.

I play this game every night in VR. I LOVE IT.  

There are a ton of tables, and I love that I can use my VR headset (and now that I've played in VR, I can't play pinball any other way. It's just so good.) 

Zaccaria Pinball doesn't have all the recognizable tables from my youth, but there's a hell of a lot of fun here. The physics are fantastic, like the best out there for a pinball simulation, and the tables are well designed. 

Some of the voice acting is kind of bland on the earlier Remakes, (sounding like a guy sitting at his desk doing a voice over, saying in a very unenthusiastic voice "bonus" and "double bonus" "skill shot" etc.) I really want better voices. 

I would also love to see build-up modes that do something really special with the table. A good example is Black Out by Williams. That's not in this game, but that rather simple 80s pinball had a mode where once you got all the lights lit up on the eject hole, the game said in a robot voice: Blackout. Then all the lights went out with this very cool electronic sound, and they came back on and gave you a big score or something. 

The build-up modes in this game don't seem to give you a big payoff visually or audibly. Plus, some are super hard to get. Being difficult to accomplish, however, isn't such a bad thing as it keeps you coming back for more. 

Other than that, the original tables, the remakes, the special tables, and now the new Deluxe and Award ones are being created... It's a dream come true for any pinball fan. My minor gripes don't take away from the full experience. A lot of love was put into this game and all the tables, and if you love pinball, you'll love this. I don't have anything to say about the retro tables since I don't like any retro pinball tables (pre solid-state). They're just not much fun in general for me, but they are very well done nonetheless. 


UPDATE: I just wanted to add this. As of Feb 2025, they have been adding new Deluxe tables for ridiculously low cost. I buy every table they create. These 2025 Deluxe and Award tables, however, are SO well done. Every table they make is well done, but these new ones are blowing me away. The layouts are super, and the music is great. The small animations they added are subtle and cool (subtle is good, because you still believe you're playing real pinball). These are the best tables they've made so far. 

Their new Tropical Deluxe table, though not my favorite theme (I prefer sci-fi or darker themes, which they have as well), has a fantastic layout, groovy music, and great shots all around. I'm THRILLED to see the team making new tables. They have made really good use of the space they are working in. 

And, I'm happy to say, the voice-overs are now more professional sounding (though, I wish some were more appropriate for the tables. Two examples: Moon Flight Deluxe sounds like a New York pizza maker and not a space pilot, and I can't stand the goofy voice on Supersonic.) 

Magic Pixel knows pinball in and out. I enjoy every table I play and love the online leaderboard option to give me a higher score to shoot for. Their entire collection today will keep me happy for years, and they're STILL adding more. Loving every minute of it.

The collection of tables is like having an arcade of over a 140 pinball tables. I can't speak highly enough. I play Zaccaria Pinball more than any other game I own.

UPDATE 2: Nominated Zaccaria Pinball for best VR game and best sit back and relax game of 2025 for the Steam Awards. I play this almost daily - well deserved.

This is (mostly) a very extensive tribute to Zaccaria, a very popular if not as well known in some corners of the world manufacturer.  Upon purchasing into the extensive library of content you will find quite the history of authentic recreations of their tables, as well as a unique take on licensing from other games of similar ilk of recreating classic Zaccaria tables as they might have been in newer (or older) design eras of pinball machines.
With this comes a significant pro and con of how the entire game is bought into: you have a lot of different ways to purchase tables; whether they be a la carte or in bundles.  While this gives you a lot of freedom in how selective you want to be on your spending or experience, it highlights that Steam doesn't have the best way to handle this with their DLC system and can be very confusing on what sort of purchase overlap you could do, so extra attention may need to be paid to not buy certain things more than once.
As far as the quality of the tables overall they're well crafted with significant attention to the physics down to allowing you to fine-tune many details if you so desire, or simply play on preset table configurations like 'arcade' which allows for more casual and easier to progress play or 'simulation' where they play closer to their real counterparts.  Zaccaria designed some rather unique ideas compared to other prominent manufacturers though some ideas fall a little flat in execution.  The more liberally designed homage tables are rather well constructed for the most part though a few have odd quirks that have cropped up through the years of tuning and adjusting engine physics.
Achievements, challenges, and modes are plentifull though some of it does feel a bit quantity over quality.  Many of the tables have their own unique achievement list; while a lot of them are the same for eech table and involve doing x mechanic y times with a single ball which don't always feel tuned the best, the simulation mode specific ones are the real fun to get as they primarily revolve around obtaining table-specific bonuses and features.  The challenge modes for each table as well as the campaign mode add additional replayability and unique goals, though some of the goals they require of you seem very oddly balanced and will make you wonder how much actual control you have in actually completing them.

Overall I've personally found it to be a great purchase and value having bought into the full bundle of content.  If you're wanting to be choosier on what parts you want then I would advise prioritizing the authentic tables, then the deluxe/modernized tables as well as the original ones.  The retro tables will largely depend on your interest in VERY early pinball machine designs which while I enjoy them they may not be the most gameplay friendly experiences,   The VR and Campaign mode options will likely be very situational buys based on your interest.

Note: this game has issues with AMD GPUs, the game stopped launching tables on my desktop so I have to play this on steam deck (which still has graphical artifacts). All that aside (and it's a lot to put aside), this game is great. The UI is a little primitive but featureful, and the physics are great as simulation mode feels nicely realistic. The tables that are based on real world pinball tables (The SS and EM tables) are a bit old school but lots of fun to play, a great way to experience games you'll probably never get the chance to play in real life. The video game original table styles are a mixed bag: the retro tables are "demakes" of the real tables but don't have much going on and aren't really worth it, the remake tables are early 90s style reimaginings of real tables that are a blast to play with their modern features and more in-depth scoring methods, and the deluxe tables are remake tables that go even further than the others with flashy extra features (a bit too much for me). The fact you can demo tables and purchase them individually is great because a lot of these tables aren't going to be for everyone, but there's something here for nearly anyone who loves pinball. All in all it's a great game for pinball fans curious about older and more obscure pinball machines.
